problem_type: Desktop lane lifecycle and renderer ownership
symptom: Opening or switching a project cannot publish its saved lane history through the shadow-only IPC registration.
direct_cause: IPC subscribes only to the workspace present at application registration; commands have no renderer-bound open or close lifecycle.
class_root: The IPC boundary does not own subscription replacement and bind every command to the renderer that opened the project.
internal_only_reason: This invariant belongs to Nomi's Electron sender and committed-project authority; the pi operation contract is unchanged.
invariants: History is published immediately after open
Only the opening renderer can command a workspace
An input and its frozen context cross one owner-checked command; owner and lane are checked again after asynchronous configuration.
Only pi durable admission acknowledges a prompt; ongoing execution cannot hold approval or cancellation IPC behind it.
Task cards read current facts from ProductionRun and refresh on its domain events without doing disk I/O on token updates.
Historical and live lane handles resolve and refresh the same current ProductionRun task facts.
Project switch, delete and return to library require successful main release; a rejected close retains the owner for an explicit retry.
generality_proof: All renderer commands cross one registered handler, which owns the active sender, subscription and workspace lifecycle.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Replace subscriptions and validate renderer ownership before dispatch.
The existing domain event commit notifies current task card consumers.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: First open and project replacement both close the previous owner and publish the current snapshot.
Every prompt, approval and queue command checks the sender before accessing the workspace.
The concurrent-send and project-replacement fixtures prove each prompt captures its own composer and no delayed configuration sends into a replacement project.
Tests prove domain status/currency/cost updates, project isolation and no disk read for repeated conversation publications.
Real Electron stage4 walk compares live task facts with the same card after a full process restart.
Rejected main close throws before project lifecycle callers proceed; the owner remains until ACK. Red/green test in laneClient.test.ts.

recurrence.reason: Every project/window replacement can leave the original subscription stale.
same_class_scan: Read main.ts registration and NomiStudioApp project open/close flows
Read laneIpc.ts registration-time subscription and command dispatch

prevention.invariant: One current renderer owns one active workspace subscription.
prevention.failure_mode: Reject commands from a missing or different owner before executing them.
prevention.strategy: Bind open, close, snapshot publication and command validation at the IPC boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: Replace registration-time-only subscription; retain no fallback.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency change is needed to bind Nomi workspace ownership.

migration: Workspace lifetimes are ephemeral; saved conversations are handled separately by the stage 4 legacy migration.
residual_risks: Real Electron open/switch/close journey remains to be verified before delivery.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Electron IPC is the first shared boundary that knows both the trusted sender and the workspace lifetime.
